desc:
You are given an array of positive integers. One operation takes two adjacent elements and replaces them by a single element equal to their sum, so the array becomes one element shorter.

Return the minimum number of operations after which the array is a palindrome (it reads the same from left to right and from right to left). A single element is a palindrome.

nums = [1,4,5,1]  -> 1
nums = [1,2,3,4]  -> 3
nums = [2,3,3,2]  -> 0

In the first example merge 4 and 5 to get [1,9,1].
hints: Compare the two ends. What can you say when they are equal?
If the left end is smaller than the right end, the left end can never match unless it grows. The only way to grow it is to merge it with its right neighbour. Doing that now never hurts.
Use two pointers with the current end sums a and b. If a == b move both pointers inward; if a < b absorb the next element on the left (one operation); otherwise absorb the next element on the right.
editorial: The final array corresponds to cutting the original into contiguous blocks whose sums read as a palindrome, and the number of operations is n minus the number of blocks. Build the blocks from both ends at once. If the left block sum equals the right block sum, close both blocks and continue inside. If the left sum is smaller, no block ending earlier on the right can match it, so the left block must absorb its right neighbour, costing one operation; symmetrically on the right.
This forced choice is why the greedy is optimal: a smaller side has no alternative. When the pointers meet, whatever is left forms the middle block. One pass, O(n) time, O(1) space.
